title: iPhone 15 screen replacement
diagnosis: Your front glass is cracked, so we'll swap the whole display assembly. This is a hard repair, so go slowly and keep your screws organized.
safety_notes: Power the phone off before opening it.
Wear safety glasses and cover the cracked glass with clear tape to avoid cuts and flying shards.
Do not use the phone if the battery looks swollen, and stop if it does.
Never pry near the battery or puncture it.

steps.title: Power off and tape the glass
steps.instruction: Hold the side button and a volume button, then slide to power off. Cover the cracked glass with clear tape.
steps.expected_visual_state: The screen is black and the front glass is covered with overlapping strips of clear tape.
common_mistakes: Only locking the screen instead of fully powering off
Leaving glass uncovered so shards fall off while working

steps.title: Remove the pentalobe screws
steps.instruction: Use the P2 pentalobe screwdriver to remove the two screws beside the USB-C port. Place them in a tray.
steps.expected_visual_state: The two screw holes beside the USB-C port are empty and the screws sit in a tray.
common_mistakes: Using the wrong screwdriver and stripping the screw heads
Losing the tiny screws

steps.title: Lift the display slightly
steps.instruction: Warm the edges of the display, then place the suction handle near the bottom edge and pull gently. Slide an opening pick into the gap.
steps.expected_visual_state: A small gap is visible along the bottom edge of the display with a pick inserted.
common_mistakes: Pulling too hard and opening the display too far
Inserting the pick deep and damaging cables
Putting the suction cup on cracked glass without tape so it will not hold

steps.title: Disconnect the battery
steps.instruction: Open the display like a book to the left, without straining the cables. Remove the battery connector bracket and unlatch the battery connector with the spudger.
steps.expected_visual_state: The display stands slightly open and the battery connector bracket is removed with the connector lifted from its socket.
common_mistakes: Skipping battery disconnection before touching other connectors
Opening the display past 90 degrees and tearing the display flex
Prying at the battery itself instead of the connector

steps.title: Remove the display connector bracket
steps.instruction: Unscrew the four tri-point screws on the display connector bracket and lift it off. Disconnect the display and Face ID connectors with the spudger.
steps.expected_visual_state: The bracket is removed and the display is held by nothing but is lying free of the frame.
common_mistakes: Mixing up screws of different lengths
Pulling the flex cables instead of unlatching the connectors by their sides

steps.title: Transfer the earpiece and sensors
steps.instruction: Move the earpiece speaker, front sensor parts and any brackets from the old display to the new one as needed. Match the position of each part carefully.
steps.expected_visual_state: The new display has the earpiece mesh and sensor parts mounted in the same positions as the old one.
common_mistakes: Damaging the delicate earpiece mesh
Forgetting to move the proximity sensor parts or dust shield

steps.title: Connect the new display
steps.instruction: Press the display and Face ID connectors into their sockets and refit the connector bracket with its four screws. Reconnect the battery connector and its bracket.
steps.expected_visual_state: The new display is connected, both brackets are screwed down, and the battery connector is seated flat.
common_mistakes: Connectors not fully clicked in, causing a black screen or no touch
Closing the phone before testing

steps.title: Close and fasten
steps.instruction: Lower the display onto the frame and press the edges until it clicks into place. Refit the two pentalobe screws.
steps.expected_visual_state: The display sits flush with the frame all around and the two screws are back beside the USB-C port.
common_mistakes: Letting a cable get pinched under the display
Forcing the display down when a connector is not seated

steps.title: Test the new screen
steps.instruction: Power on the phone and check the display, touch and Face ID. Swipe across the full screen and test the earpiece.
steps.expected_visual_state: The phone shows the Apple logo, then the lock screen, with the display bright, uncracked and responding to touch across the whole screen.
common_mistakes: Not testing touch in all corners
Ignoring a Face ID or earpiece problem until later
